title: Quality control in sublinear time: a case study via random graphs
abstract: arXiv:2508.16531v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many algorithms are designed to work well on average over inputs. But when such an algorithm is run on an arbitrary input, the question arises: Can we trust the algorithm on this input? This question is especially relevant in network science, where algorithms for theoretical random graph models are often applied to individual real-world networks.   We identify a new class of algorithmic problems addressing this, which we call "Quality Control Problems." These problems are specified by a "quality function" $\rho$ and a distribution $D$ such that, with high probability, a sample drawn from $D$ is "high quality," meaning its $\rho$-value is near $1$. The goal is to accept most inputs $x \sim D$ and reject potentially adversarially generated inputs $x$ with $\rho(x)$ far from $1$.   In this work, we consider the sublinear version of the quality control problem, where $D \in \Delta(\{0,1\}^N)$ and the goal is to solve the $(D,\rho)$

translated_title: 次线性时间中的质量控制：以随机图为案例研究
translated_abstract: 许多算法被设计为在输入总体上平均表现良好。但当这类算法在某个任意输入上运行时，问题随之而来：我们能在这个输入上信任该算法吗？这一问题在网络科学领域尤为相关，因为基于理论随机图模型的算法常常被应用于单个真实世界的网络。我们识别出一类解决此问题的新型算法问题，称之为“质量控制问题”。这类问题由一个“质量函数”$\rho$和一个分布$D$定义，使得从$D$中抽取的样本以高概率为“高质量”，即其$\rho$值接近1。目标是接受大多数来自$x \sim D$的输入，同时拒绝可能以对抗方式生成的、其$\rho(x)$远离1的输入$x$。在本工作中，我们考虑质量控制问题的次线性版本，其中$D \in \Delta(\{0,1\}^N)$，目标是求解$(D,\rho)$问题……
tldr: 该论文提出了一类新的算法问题——“质量控制问题”，研究如何在次线性时间内判断任意输入是否为高质量（即能否信任算法在该输入上的表现），并以随机图作为案例进行研究。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a new class of algorithmic problems called "Quality Control Problems," studying how to determine in sublinear time whether an arbitrary input is high-quality (i.e., whether an algorithm can be trusted on it), using random graphs as a case study.
